title: Kmart debuts iconic Korean beauty brand in store: 'Favourite' - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia
text:
Kmart expands Korean beauty offering with first-ever makeup brand from $15: 'Favourite' - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia Search query for Search the web Search the web Skip to main 
 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Kmart expands Korean beauty offering with first-ever makeup brand from $15: 'Favourite'
 The budget retailer has been stocking only Korean skincare, but that's about to change with the introduction of Colorgram.
 Claudia Poposki Thu 29 October 2026 at 6:00 am UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Kmart is bringing Colorgram to stores from November. (Yahoo Lifestyle/Getty) Kmart is expanding its Korean beauty offering to include makeup for the first time, as Aussies continue to lap up products from the country.
 The retailer already stocked an array of Korean-based skincare products , which launched earlier this year, but Cologram will be the first of a much bigger direction Kmart is taking .
 Nicola Farrell, Kmart's beauty buyer, told Yahoo Lifestyle that shoppers will notice the new products on shelves from November.
 "We're really excited about it and confident that this is the next platform for growth for us," she said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I feel like we've had an incredible six months on skincare exclusively. Our customers really responded to it.
 "People know and trust the brands we're bringing in. But there's more in the tank."
 Do you have a story? Get in touch claudia.poposki@yahooinc.com 
 What K-beauty makeup products will land at Kmart in November?
 Colorgram was launched in 2018 by CJ Olive Young and is primarily targeted at Gen Z and teens.
 The range, as the name implies, is all about bringing a pop of colour to your makeup look.
 From next month, Kmart will be stocking products ranging from $15 to $30 such as:
 Fruity Glass Tint Deep Glaze
 Fruity Glass Tint Milk
 Tin Tin Dory Cotton Blusher
 Nude Blur Tint
 All-in-one Aegyo-sal Maker Eyeshadow
 Reforming Contour Stick
 It's a huge move for Kmart, which is already looking at including other Korean beauty products to its stores.
 (Yahoo Lifestyle) RELATED: 
 Korea's 'number one' selling beauty item makes Aussie debut at Kmart, Target, Coles

 Aussie calls out 'insulting' tipping trend creeping into restaurant and cafes 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The products have received rave reviews from customers who have bought them from other retailers.
 "The fruity tint is really pretty and long-lasting," one said.
 "Their eyeliners are my absolute fave, and I love the original multi cube palette," another added.
 Nicola told Yahoo Lifestyle that Kmart is "dipping its toe" into the Korean makeup space with this initial launch, but expansion plans are already underway, and they're looking into body and hair care ranges.
 Colorgram was founded in 2018, and up until this point Kmart has only had Korean skincare.
 (Yahoo Lifestyle) Why are Aussie retailers going all in on K-beauty?
 Australia is the largest purchaser of Korean beauty products  outside Korea, and it's clear retailers are taking that statistic into account.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In September, K-beauty brand The Face Shop launched at Kmart , Coles and Target .
 This finally brought its popular Rice Water Bright range, which included the $16 cleansing wipes, a $25 light cleansing oil, and a $16.99 cleansing foam, to stores around the country.
 In August, Big W announced it would be stocking 88 Korean beauty brands, including Biodance, Medicube, TirTir, Beauty of Joseon and TORRIDEN.
 "We're constantly on the lookout for the latest must-have brands to bring to our stores, because Aussies shouldn't have to search far and wide or pay premium prices for globally trending products," Big W senior category manager Svet Rodgers said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Market research firm Credence Research found the Australian K-beauty market was worth about $149 million in 2023, and that was set to grow to $303 million by 2032.
